items.title: fix(cron): run keeps owner-private memory after its requester loses o…
items.summary: fix(cron): run keeps owner-private memory after its requester loses owner status (#198697) * fix(cron): recheck the requester's owner status when a run starts A fired condition can wait a long time for a run slot after its occurrence was admitted. Each run minted the owner bit captured at admission, so a requester who lost owner status during the wait still got an owner context, and with it owner-private memory. Each run now reads the bit again from the requester's existing owner check against the live config. Refs #196859 * test(cron): cover owner removal through a published config on both memory runtimes

items.title: fix(bonjour): Bonjour discovery fails on npm installs of 2026.11.5 be…
items.summary: fix(bonjour): Bonjour discovery fails on npm installs of 2026.11.5 betas (#199156) * fix(bonjour): ship patched Ciao as a self-contained npm bundle The core Bonjour advertiser imports @homebridge/ciao/native.js, an entry that only exists in the patched Ciao (patches/@homebridge__ciao@1.3.12.patch). The root npm package declared Ciao as an ordinary dependency, so npm installs of 2026.11.5-beta.1 and beta.2 resolved the registry package without native.js and Bonjour failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Bundle the patched Ciao in the root package, as the Bonjour plugin package already does, and make the tarball check require bundling whenever dist imports the patched entry. Bundling alone is not enough: npm packs a pnpm-linked bundle's installed dependencies at their store path (node_modules/.pnpm/.../node_modules/debug), where the relocated bundle cannot resolve them and the tarball check rejects them. Packing now restages any linked bundle that has installed dependencies into a flat npm layout and drops the leftover store entries, so Ciao ships with debug, fast-deep-equal, source-map-support and tslib next to it. Refs #198010 Refs #198011 Co-authored-by: Alfred J Berchtold Co-authored-by: alfredjbclaw * fix(package): restage only bundles npm packed under their pnpm store entry The first cut restaged every pnpm-linked bundle with installed dependencies. That also restaged @openclaw/ai, whose dependencies the root package already installs, and pulled its whole transitive closure into the tarball (346,027 installed entries). Restage a linked bundle only when npm actually left its dependencies under that bundle's pnpm store entry in the packed root; other packed bundles stay as npm wrote them. Refs #198010 --------- Co-authored-by: Alfred J Berchtold Co-authored-by: alfredjbclaw
